tolerance.source: Plan section 7: a test counts as near a habitat when it is within 0.05 O2 fraction and 20 kPa of the target box.

scenarios.label: ISS and Earth-normal cabin
scenarios.source: Challenge text: Earth's pressure at sea level is 14.7 psi (101.3 kPa). The ISS cabin runs close to sea-level air.
assumptions: The ISS box is sea-level air with a small margin. The challenge does not state the ISS atmosphere directly.

scenarios.label: Lunar base
scenarios.source: Challenge text: the intermediate oxygen concentration used on the Moon will likely be 30% or greater, with a corresponding pressure of 10.2 psi (70.3 kPa) or less, between a spacesuit (4.3 psi, 29.6 kPa) and Earth's atmosphere.
assumptions: The 40% upper O2 bound is ours. The challenge only gives the lower bound.

scenarios.label: Pressurized rover
scenarios.source: Challenge text: the Moon Base and pressurized rover(s) will be at a pressure and oxygen concentration between those in a spacesuit and the Earth's atmosphere.
assumptions: Same box as the lunar base, as the challenge groups them together.

scenarios.label: Mars habitat
scenarios.source: No atmosphere is given for Mars in the challenge.
assumptions: Our assumption: a Mars habitat uses the same reduced-pressure, oxygen-enriched atmosphere as the lunar base.

scenarios.label: Spacesuit
scenarios.source: Challenge text: spacesuits are filled with 100% oxygen to only 4.3 psi (29.6 kPa).
assumptions: Context only. No PSI test comes close, so this shows the size of the data gap.
